phases.title: Project structure and build-state system
phases.block: Block A - Foundations (the walking skeleton)
phases.intent: Create the shape the whole project lives in, and the state system that lets any session - here, or Cursor on the work machine - know where the build is without reading a conversation. No domain logic at all.
tasks: Repo tree matching the blueprint's own repo listing, every directory with an __init__.py and a README saying what belongs there and what does not
uv toolchain: pyproject.toml, Python 3.12 pinned, uv.lock committed
ruff + pytest + mypy configured in pyproject, no separate config files
BUILD/: plan.json as truth, PLAN.md and STATE.md generated, LEDGER.md and AMENDMENTS.md append-only
tools/gate.py: status, check, close, checkpoint, amend, ledger, render
CLAUDE.md at the repo root carrying the session rules
tests/p01 asserting the structure is what the blueprint says it is
exit: Every directory in the blueprint repo tree exists and carries a README
uv sync reproduces the environment from a clean checkout
gate status prints the cursor with no arguments
gate close P02 refuses, because P02 has not been built
The gate tests derive their targets from plan.json rather than naming a phase, so they stay true as phases close
The blueprint is authoritative in the repo, and sync_blueprint.py publishes to the mirror rather than pulling from it
BUILD/phases/PNN.md are generated by gate render from plan.json, not maintained by hand
Each package names the phase that first builds it, and the ahead-of-plan check binds only packages whose phase has not been reached
phases.notes: The refusal test matters more than it looks. A check-off mechanism that cannot refuse is decoration.

phases.title: Contracts and registries
phases.block: Block A - Foundations (the walking skeleton)
phases.intent: Every shape the system passes around, defined once, versioned, and enforced at the boundary rather than restated per skill. Includes the two configuration-sourced inputs a pre-build review found had no producer.
tasks: figure.schema.json - the envelope: value, unit, currency, scale, period, source_id, locator, source_version, derivation, masked, confidence, produced_by, model_pin
One output schema per skill, referencing the envelope rather than restating it
event.schema.json and run_manifest.schema.json
engagement_profile.schema.json (finding F1): industry classification, size band, fiscal calendar, scale convention, owner-compensation baseline, disposition
participant_census as a declared intake document type
constraints.yaml - the predicates the Policy Gate evaluates
A registry loader that pins version and refuses an unknown one
registries/ package: the loaders for contracts, constraints and (from P07) diagnostics
exit: Every schema loads, self-validates, and carries a version in its id
A figure missing scale is rejected; scale is never inferred downstream
A figure citing source_id 'derived', 'model' or 'analysis' is rejected as fabricated provenance
engagement_profile round-trips and a profile missing owner-compensation baseline fails validation
phases.notes: F1 lands here. Three skills declare engagement_profile and nothing produced it - the fix is a contract, because invariant 23 already decided configuration writes the engagement record.

phases.title: Ports and adapters, with one conformance suite
phases.block: Block A - Foundations (the walking skeleton)
phases.intent: Six interfaces and their local adapters, plus a single suite every adapter must pass. This is what makes adding ShareFile later a class rather than a refactor.
tasks: Six Protocols under ports/, each with the narrowest surface that works
storage: local_folder adapter. delivery: local_folder adapter
secrets: dotenv adapter, reading presence never printing value
queue: in_process adapter
llm: a fake adapter that replays recorded fixtures, so phases 4-10 need no API key
One conformance suite, parameterised over every registered adapter
An import-boundary test: nothing outside ports/ imports an adapter directly
ports/compute: a Protocol and a local_process adapter, so the run manifest can record where the work happened
exit: All six ports have a Protocol and at least one adapter
The conformance suite passes for every registered adapter
No module outside ports/ imports a concrete adapter
Switching AA_STORAGE_ADAPTER changes behaviour with no pipeline code touched
phases.notes: The ShareFile and Box connectors that exist at work become adapters here at handoff. Nothing before P25 depends on them.

phases.title: Event bus, run store, manifest
phases.block: Block A - Foundations (the walking skeleton)
phases.intent: The record. Every guard writes to it, passes included, so silence is never ambiguous - and the manifest is written unconditionally, including when a run halts.
tasks: SQLAlchemy models: run, step, event, artifact, review_item, decision
A repository port over the store, so SQLite and Postgres are one URL apart
Append-only event bus - no update path exists in the API at all
Manifest writer wired to run end regardless of outcome
The seven run states: queued, running, waiting, quarantined, halted, delivered, superseded
exit: A halted run still writes a complete manifest
The event table has no update path reachable from application code
All seven run states are reachable and asserted in tests
The store conformance suite is parameterised over SQLite and Postgres, passes on SQLite, and reports the Postgres run as not-run rather than skipping it silently when no server is reachable
phases.notes: SQLite for phases 1-24 behind the repository port; the Postgres run is what stops SQLite-only SQL creeping in unnoticed.

phases.title: Scope resolver
phases.block: Block B - The engine
phases.intent: Five-layer resolution, deeper shadows shallower, overlays may only tighten. This is what makes 'an engagement can only see the skills its scope resolves to' true by construction rather than by policy.
tasks: scopes.yaml - practice groups, segments, dispositions
LAYER_ORDER: _firm, <practice>/_group, <practice>/_<disposition>, <practice>/<segment>/_segment, <practice>/<segment>/<disposition>
The resolver, returning exactly one skill set per scope path
The skill index: name and description only, never a skill body
Overlay merge with a tighten-only assertion that raises on a loosening
exit: An overlay that lowers a HITL requirement or widens a privacy class raises
Consulting resolves to the firm layer only, and the resolver says so explicitly
The skill index never contains a skill body or a reference file
Every scope combination the declared taxonomy admits - eight today, including the one no engagement uses yet - resolves to exactly one skill set, with no skill in it twice
phases.notes: The same resolver binds Excel model templates per practice group - one mechanism, two kinds of artifact.

phases.title: Graph compiler
phases.block: Block B - The engine
phases.intent: Turn a named job recipe into a typed DAG with a plan hash. Nothing executes that has not been through here.
tasks: The frozen Step dataclass: id, kind, skill, inputs, output_schema, timeout_s, retries, loop, on_failure, max_turns
Named job recipes in YAML, compiled to a DAG
Topological ordering and parallel-branch identification
Declared loop regions with an integer ceiling; undeclared cycles rejected
plan_hash over structure, skill versions, model pins, template version, taxonomy version, schema versions and the precedent-store snapshot id
exit: An undeclared cycle is rejected at compile time with a locatable error
Identical inputs and configuration give an identical plan_hash
Changing the precedent-store snapshot changes the plan_hash
max_turns defaults to 1, and a step declaring more is rejected
phases.notes: Recipes, not a model, produce the plan until P26. Debugging plan compilation and a model's plan proposal at the same time means trusting neither.

phases.title: The assertion suites
phases.block: Block B - The engine
phases.intent: The 25 invariants become tests that run in CI and before every execution, rather than properties of a picture that can be quietly wrong for months.
tasks: Export the blueprint's node and edge model to graph/architecture.json, checked into the repo
architecture_assertions.py over that graph - the CI suite
plan_assertions.py over a compiled plan - runs before every execute
All 25 invariants expressed, including invariant 23 as a real graph walk and invariant 24 as reachability
Wire both suites into gate check
exit: All 25 invariants are executable and pass against the current architecture
Deleting an edge in a fixture graph makes exactly the right assertion fail
Plan assertions run before execute and refuse a plan that violates one
assert_all_loops_bounded enforces max_turns == 1 on every skill step
phases.notes: Two graphs, two suites. Conflating the 118-node architecture graph with the ~8-step plan graph is what made three assertions unsatisfiable in the blueprint's first draft.

phases.title: Step executor, idempotency, resume
phases.block: Block B - The engine
phases.intent: A retry, a crash resume and a manual re-run after a fix are the same operation - and only the steps whose inputs actually changed are paid for twice.
tasks: step_key = sha256(step_id, input content hashes, skill@version, model_pin, context_ref, output_schema_version)
The idempotency ledger, written inside the same transaction as the step result
Execute at the frontier: completed steps satisfied from the ledger
Per-step timeout, one transport retry, then quarantine
A blocked run checkpoints and exits - no process, no lock, no context window held
exit: Killing a run mid-flight and resuming re-executes zero completed steps
A late result from a timed-out step cannot overwrite the retry that replaced it
A run blocked on a review item releases its lock and stops the wall-clock budget
Steps pass content-addressed refs, never values
phases.notes: The checkpoint-and-exit decision is what makes the '4h excluding time waiting on a human' budget honest.

phases.title: Context builder
phases.block: Block B - The engine
phases.intent: Everything a model is shown is assembled in one place and recorded, so any call can be reconstructed exactly.
tasks: Assemble skill body, declared references, firm standards, retrieved precedents, engagement_profile and the masked payload
Content-hash the assembled whole into context_ref
Persist the assembled context against the run
Progressive disclosure: reference files loaded only once a skill is selected
exit: context_ref reproduces the exact bytes a model was shown
Changing a retrieved precedent changes context_ref and therefore step_key
A skill body is never loaded for a skill the plan did not select
Precedent retrieval is scope-built and cannot cross an engagement boundary
phases.notes: context_ref in the idempotency key was a correction: without it a resumed run could return a cached result the current context would no longer produce.

phases.title: Policy gate, constraints, guarded runtime
phases.block: Block C - The harness around one step
phases.intent: A wrong action can produce a right-looking result. Verification catches a wrong result; only a decision taken before execution catches a wrong act.
tasks: ProposedAction and the four allow conditions: declared tool, args satisfy every predicate, engagement matches, estimated cost within remaining budget
constraints.yaml predicates evaluated, not interpreted
The six-name tool namespace (finding F3): recompute and timing_normalizer compute; chart_of_accounts_lookup, precedent_lookup, index_lookup and template_schema_lookup read
Every denial recorded as an event with a code and an owner
Call-time caps applied by the runtime, not trusted from the caller
exit: A tool not in the caller's allowlist is denied and the denial is in the event stream
An argument naming another engagement is denied
A gated read is authorised exactly as a write is
A test proves no module under skills/ can import anything under tools/
phases.notes: t_template is deliberately in no skill's allowlist: model-load emits a mapping, the Template Writer executes it. A skill that could write cells could write one the mapping never declared.

phases.title: LLM port, model pin, budget governor
phases.block: Block C - The harness around one step
phases.intent: One door to a model and one request per step. Per finding F4 this is the Messages API - SKILL.md is a file format we parse, not a framework dependency.
tasks: Anthropic Messages adapter behind the LLM port
A SKILL.md parser: frontmatter, body, reference list - our own, owing nothing to any SDK
Model pin including effort; the three tiers (claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5)
max_turns == 1 enforced at the call site, not merely asserted in the plan
Outbound payload scan on the one door
Token and cost meter, and the four budget ceilings
exit: A call attempting more than one model turn raises before it is sent
Every outbound payload passes the scan, and the scan's fixture (a stubbed no-op masker) is caught
Each of the four ceilings halts and escalates in a test
The cost meter agrees with the usage the API reports
phases.notes: F4 lands here. The Agent SDK's cited benefits - subagent loops, SDK-dispatched tools - are exactly what single-turn removes. It stays available as an adapter behind this port.

phases.title: Privacy: mask, vault, unmask, verify
phases.block: Block C - The harness around one step
phases.intent: Tokens stable per engagement, re-identification deterministic, and no model node anywhere near the vault. The value here is cross-client isolation and precedent portability, not provider trust.
tasks: Masker over account names and identifying strings
Per-engagement vault with a retention field, the only store that can re-identify anything
Deterministic unmask in Python - no model has an unmask tool
Unmask integrity check as a separate node from the masker, so the check can be tested independently of the thing it checks
exit: The same account masks to the same token across runs weeks apart - period alignment depends on this
A token issued under a different engagement_id fails the integrity check
Zero residual mask tokens in any released artifact
A graph assertion proves no llm-exec node reaches the vault
phases.notes: Masking is step 2 of management's own Model Builder. Analyst Chat is the one model surface deliberately outside this path.

phases.title: Guards and their adversarial fixtures
phases.block: Block C - The harness around one step
phases.intent: Five assertions about the figure envelope, each with a fixture built specifically to defeat it. A guard with no adversarial fixture is an assumption.
tasks: Output schema validator, provenance check, tie-out check, reconciliation, numeric integrity lock
The recompute engine, reading the Source Parse Store rather than trusting a stated total
The ten adversarial fixtures from the blueprint's fixture table
Every guard emits on pass as well as on failure
exit: Each of the ten fixtures fires the right guard, and only that guard
A total altered by 0.4% fails tie-out - plausible on sight, outside tolerance
A figure citing source_id 'derived' fails provenance
A template writer that rounds to the nearest thousand fails the numeric lock
phases.notes: Tie-out proves arithmetic, not selection. Eight wrong rows added correctly still pass here; selection is caught by materiality review, the self-verification pass and the sampling audit.

phases.title: Loop controller, quarantine, diagnostics
phases.block: Block C - The harness around one step
phases.intent: Failure converges on a person or a record, never on silence - and every loop has a maximum you can read off the plan before the run starts.
tasks: Bounded loop regions with the four in-run loops: guard repair (2), tie-out repair (1), self-verification (1), conflict resolution (1)
The input-must-change rule - a retry with unchanged input is the same call at the same price
Quarantine holding full context, with independent branches allowed to finish
The diagnostic namespace: code, owner, expected, found, what_now
exit: A skill returning byte-identical output is stopped rather than retried
Loop exhaustion quarantines and opens a review item carrying both positions
Every error code in the namespace has an owner and a what_now
Nothing partial is ever released from a quarantined run
phases.notes: Only in-run loops live in a plan. Human clarification is a suspend-and-resume; drift re-review is human-paced across runs. Implementing all three in one mechanism is the mistake the scope column prevents.

phases.title: Confidence router, review queue, decision log
phases.block: Block C - The harness around one step
phases.intent: Decides what a person sees, item by item, and makes their answer the only thing in the system that can write a precedent.
tasks: Materiality thresholds and the auto-accept confidence bar, both per engagement
Checkpoint policy that may only tighten, never loosen a skill's floor
Review queue with an SLA and a named owner per engagement
Review surface API and the decision log
Optimistic locking so two reviewers cannot silently overwrite each other
exit: A policy attempting to lower a skill's review floor is rejected
A material item is queued regardless of confidence
The second reviewer on an item sees the first's decision rather than overwriting it
A recorded decision re-enqueues the waiting run at its frontier
phases.notes: 'Nobody works the queue' is the second-highest risk in the blueprint and it is not technical. The SLA and the stall alert are the only defences the system itself can offer.

phases.title: Intake: roster, sweep, binding, lock, window
phases.block: Block D - First real vertical, local end to end
phases.intent: What gets looked at, when a run actually starts, and the guarantee that an inactive engagement is unreachable rather than merely unchecked.
tasks: The roster and its three states: active, paused, archived
Sweep planner reading the roster - the only thing that decides what is swept
Pattern watches (one row, forty clients) and bound watches, with unmatched folders routed to a person and never guessed
Fingerprinting, sha256 source_id, and source_version on re-upload
Engagement binding that fails closed before anything is read, and the per-engagement lock
Intake window: quiet_period 30 min, required_types from the recipe, max_wait 24 h
exit: Invariant 24 proven by graph walk: no path from any intake source into the pipeline for an off-roster engagement
Six files arriving over ten minutes produce one run, not six
A re-uploaded file becomes source_version 2 and supersedes the earlier run without overwriting its manifest
Two runs launched on one engagement in the same second serialise on the lock
phases.notes: A run consumes the whole current intake set, never a delta - a delta is not a valid input to timing normalization or tagging.

phases.title: Readers and the Source Parse Store
phases.block: Block D - First real vertical, local end to end
phases.intent: Turn files into an addressable parse that provenance and tie-out can read from - the store finding F2 showed nothing owned.
tasks: pypdf and python-docx extraction, attaching source_id and a page/table/row locator to every emitted item
Workbook reader: structural read of names and headers, one model call selects sheets with reasons, deterministic code normalizes only those
Document classifier and the period/scale detector, with an explicit ambiguous flag rather than an assumption
The untrusted content boundary
The Source Parse Store keyed (run_id, source_id, locator), written once by the readers and never updated, plus its locator resolver
exit: Every extracted figure resolves by (source_id, locator) through one interface, whatever kind of file it came from
Every skipped sheet is reported with a reason
A PDF carrying instructions in 1pt white text and zero-width characters reaches a model as data, not as instructions
Scale ambiguity is reported and never assumed - thousands versus units is the most expensive silent error available here
phases.notes: F2 lands here. Provenance, tie-out and the numeric lock are all assertions about source rows, and none can be written until something owns the rows.

phases.title: First real skill: timing normalization
phases.block: Block D - First real vertical, local end to end
phases.human_check: You confirm the alignment the system proposes on a real engagement is one you would have made yourself - and that every unmatched line it reported is genuinely unmatched.
phases.intent: The first real skill, chosen first because its arithmetic is entirely deterministic: the model proposes an alignment and the tool does every calculation.
tasks: SKILL.md with frontmatter, procedure, when-to-use, when-not-to-use, escalation
Reference files: period-conventions.md, line-item-matching.md
The alignment proposal schema - a mapping, never a number
t_timing executing the mapping; all arithmetic in the tool
Golden fixtures plus the alignment-report fixture set
exit: 100% arithmetic agreement with the deterministic tool
At least 98% line-item match rate on the fixture set
Every unmatched line reported, and no period gap interpolated
A file flagged ambiguous by the period detector escalates before the skill proceeds
phases.notes: First skill on purpose: if the model is wrong here the tool disagrees immediately, so the feedback loop is short and mechanical.

phases.title: Line-item tagging and the precedent store
phases.block: Block E - Real skills and their surfaces
phases.human_check: You review the 400-item fixture disagreements yourself and confirm the gold set is right where the system and the gold set differ.
phases.intent: The highest-volume skill in the system, and the first one that learns - which is exactly why only a human decision can write to what it learns from.
tasks: Firm chart-of-accounts taxonomy, versioned
The skill: Category, Excluded from A/L, Include in NWC, with confidence and a one-line rationale per item
Scope-built precedent retrieval - a repeat client sees its own prior decisions first
Write-back gated on a decision id, with no other code path into the store
exit: At least 95% top-1 agreement with the analyst gold set over a 400-item fixture
Zero provenance failures
No code path writes a precedent without a human decision id
Retrieval cannot cross an engagement scope boundary, proven by test not by convention
phases.notes: A system that learns from its own unreviewed output drifts, and does it invisibly. The single-writer rule is the whole defence.

phases.title: EBITDA normalization
phases.block: Block E - Real skills and their surfaces
phases.human_check: You confirm the add-backs proposed on a real engagement are defensible, and that nothing material was auto-accepted.
phases.intent: The first skill where a mistake is expensive rather than merely visible - which is why it is high tier, always self-verified, and never auto-accepts anything material.
tasks: Add-back taxonomy and officer-compensation tests with a cited benchmark
recompute called on every proposed amount
The self-verification pass as a separate invocation that never sees the first pass's reasoning
Materiality routing: above the threshold goes to review regardless of confidence
engagement_profile consumed for the owner-compensation baseline (the F1 contract)
exit: 100% of proposed add-backs tie via recompute
At least 90% recall against analyst-identified add-backs on the fixture
No add-back above the materiality threshold is ever auto-accepted
A candidate recurring across all periods is escalated, not proposed
phases.notes: Never applies an add-back - proposes it with evidence. There is no field in the schema for a concluded value.

phases.title: Model builder, template registry, release
phases.block: Block E - Real skills and their surfaces
phases.intent: openpyxl into a copy of a pinned template, bound by named range and never by cell address. One node releases client work, with one inbound edge.
tasks: Template registration: introspect the workbook, list its declared named ranges, assert every required mapping input is present
The CONFIG.TEMPLATE_INPUTS_MISSING diagnostic with code, owner and what_now
Model-load emitting a mapping; the Template Writer performing every write
Deliverable QC: opens, resolves, stamped, no residual tokens, no broken external link, no #REF!
The single release gate and the idempotency ledger record inside the release transaction
Workpaper narrative, written after the numbers are locked, with no schema field a figure can enter through
exit: A binding to a cell address is rejected at registration
A template declaring 41 of 43 required inputs fails registration naming the two missing ranges
A produced .xlsx opens with no #REF!, no broken link and no residual mask token
A replayed release does not deliver a second time
phases.notes: Read the model builder repo from work before writing the Template Writer - it may already solve the named-range binding, and it is the one existing repo that overlaps this phase.

phases.title: Eval and replay harnesses
phases.block: Block F - Assurance and operations
phases.intent: Fixtures only cover cases somebody thought of. Replay answers the question fixtures cannot: would this candidate have changed anything real?
tasks: Golden fixtures per skill plus the adversarial fixtures per guard
The per-skill acceptance gates from the blueprint's gate table
Replay: re-run a candidate over the masked inputs of past engagements and diff against what was delivered
gate eval <skill> as a first-class command
exit: Every shipped skill has fixtures and a named numeric gate
Replay produces a diff against past deliverables, not just a pass/fail
A skill below its gate cannot be registered
Fixture coverage is reported, including what is not covered

phases.title: Ops console, scorecard, drift, stalls
phases.block: Block F - Assurance and operations
phases.intent: Every run ends with a computed verdict against versioned criteria, so no run's outcome is a matter of opinion.
tasks: FastAPI plus SSE over the event bus
The run scorecard: coverage, provenance, tie-out, conflicts, masking, numeric integrity, budget, review outstanding, deliverable QC
Versioned acceptance criteria, so 'what counted as working' is answerable for a run six months old
Drift monitor over override rate, confidence distribution and guard failure rate
Stall detection against the review SLA
exit: Every run gets a scorecard with a computed verdict
The console replays a completed run from the event stream alone
A stalled review item raises an alert against its SLA
Node state comes from explicit events, never inferred from a log line's severity

phases.title: Admin console, preflight, config audit
phases.block: Block F - Assurance and operations
phases.intent: A new engagement can be set up without touching code, and a setup error is found in a minute rather than in a halted run.
tasks: The roster, watches, destinations and model bindings as an editable surface over config_store
Model binding resolved through LAYER_ORDER - the same resolver as skills
The ten preflight checks, including engagement profile completeness (F1)
The config change log: who, what, when and why
Enforcement of what an admin can and cannot change, backed by invariant 23
exit: A failing preflight check blocks activation of that engagement rather than failing later in a run
Every preflight failure carries a code, an owner and a what_now
No configuration edge reaches a node that can fail closed, proven by graph walk
Every active engagement resolves to exactly one destination and one template pin
phases.notes: config is the most likely failure owner on a new engagement. This is the surface where those failures are prevented rather than diagnosed.

phases.title: Worker pool and the queue port
phases.block: Block G - Scale, judgment and handoff
phases.intent: A nightly sweep over seven active engagements cannot run one at a time inside a four-hour per-run ceiling.
tasks: A bounded worker pool behind the job queue port
Cross-engagement concurrency, with the engagement lock still serialising within one
Redis + RQ adapter for when runs outlive a single process
Backpressure and a visible queue position
exit: Several engagements process concurrently while one engagement still serialises
Queue position is visible on the console for a queued run
Swapping in_process for Redis changes no pipeline code
A worker dying mid-step leaves a resumable run, not a corrupt one

phases.title: Orchestrator agent and triage
phases.block: Block G - Scale, judgment and handoff
phases.human_check: You confirm the plans the orchestrator proposes on real engagements are the plans you would have chosen, across at least ten runs.
phases.intent: The model proposes a plan; it is still compiled, asserted and hashed before anything runs. This arrives last on purpose.
tasks: Orchestrator working from the skill index (name and description only) and the job manifest
Structured output: a plan proposal, never a value
The proposal goes through the same compiler and the same plan assertions as a recipe
Triage for no confident match, with a schema containing no field for a figure
Fall back to the named recipe when the proposal fails assertions
exit: A proposed plan that violates any plan assertion is rejected and the recipe is used instead
The orchestrator's context never contains a skill body, only the index
A proposal is reproducible: same inputs, same plan_hash
Triage can escalate but has no schema field in which a number could be recorded
phases.notes: Everything before this uses named recipes. Building the model-driven planner last means the verification spine is proven against a fixed plan first.

phases.title: The governance chain
phases.block: Block G - Scale, judgment and handoff
phases.intent: Skills are how this system changes, and ungoverned change is the main long-term risk. A dropped draft is a candidate, not a skill.
tasks: Drop folder, conformance check against the skill contract, adaptation bench
Authoring sandbox and its test harness, reading masked payloads only
Submit, review board, shadow deployment with a sustained agreement threshold
The registry as the single writer to the live skills/ tree
The governance record
exit: No path from the drop folder to the tree skips fixtures, review or a shadow run - remove any one gate and the path breaks
Governance reads only masked payloads and registries, never client-identifying data
Nothing reaches the skill index without passing fixtures and a shadow run
Promotion requires a sustained agreement threshold, not one good day
phases.notes: The adaptation bench can produce a conforming skill. It cannot produce fixtures - those are evidence the skill works, and evidence cannot be authored by the thing it vouches for.

phases.title: Docker, portability, handoff packet
phases.block: Block G - Scale, judgment and handoff
phases.human_check: You clone the repo onto the work machine, run the suite in the container, and confirm nothing but .env had to change.
phases.intent: One image, any host. The portability requirement in its most concrete form - and the packet that makes the move to the work machine boring.
tasks: Dockerfile and compose: app plus Postgres, one command up
The whole suite green inside the container
HANDOFF.md: what changes on the work machine and what does not
Adapter stubs named for the existing ShareFile and Box connectors, with their port contracts written
The work Anthropic key as a .env change and nothing else
exit: No managed-service primitive is depended on anywhere in the codebase
HANDOFF.md names every environment difference between this machine and the work one
A clean clone plus .env reaches a passing suite with no undocumented step

The image builds and the whole suite passes inside it with no host Python involved, using any OCI-compatible runtime - podman, containerd, Rancher Desktop or Docker Engine. No step depends on Docker Desktop, and HANDOFF.md names the runtime actually used
phases.notes: The three work repos - model builder, ShareFile connector, Box connector - are named here as adapters to write, not as dependencies to satisfy.

checkpoints.title: The skeleton holds bytes
checkpoints.proves: A fake run moves bytes storage to delivery, emits events and writes a manifest

checkpoints.title: A plan compiles and hashes
checkpoints.proves: A recipe compiles; identical inputs give an identical plan_hash and a changed precedent snapshot changes it; and the store conformance suite passes against Postgres in Docker as well as SQLite

checkpoints.title: A run survives being killed
checkpoints.proves: Kill mid-flight, resume, zero completed steps re-execute, and plan assertions gate the resume

checkpoints.title: One step through all six harness stages
checkpoints.proves: A no-op skill passes context, reason, policy, act, verify and accept, with every stage emitting

checkpoints.title: Every guard fires on its own fixture
checkpoints.proves: All ten adversarial fixtures fire the right guard, every loop is bounded, and every failure carries code, owner and what_now

checkpoints.title: The walking vertical
checkpoints.proves: Watched folder to masked payload to one real skill to guards to review to local output, on one real engagement

checkpoints.title: A deliverable an analyst would accept
checkpoints.proves: Three real skills on real files produce an .xlsx that opens clean, with every figure sourced and recomputed

checkpoints.title: Observable and self-service
checkpoints.proves: A run is fully observable from its event stream alone, and a new engagement is set up without touching code
